books.section: B. The Deepening of Partisanship in the Twenty-first Century
Threat of Terrorism, Increase of Presidential Power, and Economic Crisis (2001-2016)

stem: The Tea Party movement rose sharply after 2009. Which of the following best explains its rise?

options.text: The Tea Party formed to defend the Affordable Care Act from repeal
options.misconception: The Tea Party opposed the Affordable Care Act; defending it was the opposite of its purpose.

options.text: The Tea Party demanded higher taxes and a larger federal government
options.misconception: The Tea Party demanded the opposite — lower taxes and a smaller federal government.

options.text: Opposition to the health-care law mobilized voters who saw government as too big
The Tea Party was founded by Democratic leaders to support President Obama
options.misconception: The Tea Party was a conservative opposition movement, not a Democratic creation.

rationales.A: Background: the Tea Party opposed the Affordable Care Act; defending it was the opposite of its purpose.
rationales.B: Background: the Tea Party demanded the opposite — lower taxes and a smaller federal government.
rationales.C: Background: the election of Barack Obama and the health-care law generated a vocal opposition movement, fed by grassroots discontent with big government.
rationales.D: Background: the Tea Party was a conservative opposition movement, not a Democratic creation.
rationales.general:
1. Ask what changed in 2009: a new Democratic president, a health-care law, and big federal spending.
2. Background: the election of Barack Obama and the health-care law generated a vocal opposition movement.
3. Background: it drew on grassroots discontent with big government, amplified by sympathetic media.
4. The movement opposed the law and the spending — it never defended them or demanded more of either.
Remember: the Tea Party was the backlash to Obama's expansion of government.
